summary: Prometheus on node1 now monitors node2, node3, and node4 by hostname. All targets expose current metrics on port 9100 only to node1, while Prometheus listens exclusively on 127.0.0.1:9090. Configuration and access controls persisted through sequential restarts of every node.
actions_performed: Installed and enabled Prometheus on node1 and node_exporter on node2–node4.
Configured hostname-based targets: node2:9100, node3:9100, and node4:9100.
Restricted each exporter with persistent UFW allow-from-node1 and deny-all-other rules.
Restarted node2, node3, node4, then node1 individually, verifying full monitoring recovery before continuing.
Disabled the unsupported auto-installed OpenIPMI service; all nodes finish in systemd running state with zero failed units.

evidence.requirement: Hostname-based targets and current metrics are queryable on node1
evidence.summary: Post-restart checks show three healthy hostname targets, current node_time_seconds values, host identity series, and direct metrics from node2–node4.

evidence.requirement: Prometheus port 9090 remains local to node1
evidence.summary: Prometheus listens only on 127.0.0.1:9090; loopback readiness succeeds while node1’s managed IP and a remote node cannot connect.

evidence.requirement: Only node1 can collect each node_exporter endpoint
evidence.summary: Each exporter retained its node-IP listener and ordered allow-node1/deny-others firewall rules after reboot. node1 fetched all metrics, while non-node1 attempts against every exporter timed out.
